text_blocks.snippet: To be diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) according to the DSM-5, an individual must experience a depressed mood or loss of interest/pleasure in most activities, along with at least five other symptoms from a specific list, for a minimum of two weeks. These symptoms must represent a change from previous functioning and cause significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of life.
snippet_highlighted_words: an individual must experience a depressed mood or loss of interest/pleasure in most activities, along with at least five other symptoms from a specific list, for a minimum of two weeks

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of the DSM-5 criteria:
Core Symptoms (at least one must be present):

list.title: Depressed mood:
list.snippet: This can be reported subjectively (feeling sad, empty, hopeless) or observed by others (appearing tearful). In children and adolescents, this may present as irritability.

list.title: Loss of interest or pleasure:
list.snippet: Markedly diminished interest or pleasure in all, or almost all, activities most of the day, nearly every day.

text_blocks.snippet: Other Possible Symptoms (at least four more needed, in addition to one of the core symptoms):

list.snippet: Significant weight loss or gain: (or decrease or increase in appetite).
Insomnia or hypersomnia: nearly every day.
Psychomotor agitation or retardation: (observable by others).
Feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt .
Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness .
Recurrent thoughts of death, suicidal ideation, plans, or attempts .

list.title: Duration:
list.snippet: These symptoms must be present for at least two weeks.

list.title: Change from baseline:
list.snippet: The symptoms should represent a change from the individual's previous level of functioning.

list.title: Impairment:
list.snippet: The symptoms must cause significant impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of life.

list.title: Not due to other conditions:
list.snippet: The symptoms should not be better explained by the physiological effects of a substance or another medical condition.

list.title: No history of mania or hypomania:
list.snippet: The diagnosis of MDD is not made if the individual has ever experienced a manic or hypomanic episode.
